# OWA Robot Test — Coverage Matrix

The **complete inventory of testable UI units**, each with a stable ID. "Coverage" for
this skill is defined against this file: a run (or a chain of runs) reaches full coverage
when **every in-scope row has been exercised with evidence**. Nothing may be silently
skipped — a row is either exercised (PASS/FAIL), BLOCKED with a stated reason, or
EXCLUDED by the policy table below.

> Derived from [components-path.md](./components-path.md) + a source sweep of `src/`.
> If the app UI changes, update the matrix **and bump `matrixVersion`** (the date below)
> — and check whether the affected [user-workflows.md](./user-workflows.md) recipes
> (each cites matrix rows in its `Verify:` line) need the same update.
> Before a full run, spot-check the matrix against `src/` (new `*Comp.tsx` folders =
> new rows).

**matrixVersion: 2026-09-26** (**GL-25 expanded: the automatic Tip of the Day waits five minutes.** Reported with a picture of the card over the Presenter's top-right controls at launch. It now appears five minutes after launch, counted from the launch in session storage (`daily-tip-launched-at`), so a reload or page switch does not restart it; Help is never delayed, and a tip opened from Help stands in for the automatic one. No row-count change.)

Previous: **matrixVersion: 2026-09-25i** (**PM-146: a session's Properties act on that session's OWN overlay.** Reported straight after the strip landed. The values were already filed per session and the panel already drew the right ones; what leaked was the live restyle, which walked every overlay of that kind — so a nudge to Session 2's size or colour re-dressed the countdown Default had on the wall. Scoped to the owning session; the Hide row is deliberately NOT scoped, because there must always be a way to take something off a projector from whichever session is in front. Proven live 2026-09-25 by reading the screen's own saved style both ways round.)

Previous: **matrixVersion: 2026-09-25h** (**PM-146, PM-147: every foreground component keeps SESSIONS, not only the four that show a file.** Asked for directly, pointing at the Video Show panel's own `Default / +` strip and circling the components in the launcher menu. Messages, Marquee Top, Marquee Bottom, Quick Text, Countdown, Stopwatch and Time now carry the same strip, a session owning that panel's own words or numbers AND its own Properties — the pre-service notice board and the mid-service alert side by side, each already the right size in the right corner, instead of one retyped over the other minutes before a service. Default's suffix is the empty string, so it keeps writing the keys the widgets always wrote. The two widgets that hold a LIST (Messages, Time) can have two sessions up at once and preserve each other's items; the five single-slot ones hand the slot over and move the on-screen dot with it. Removing a session takes what it put up off the screens first. Verified live 2026-09-25 on the presenter.)

Previous: **matrixVersion: 2026-09-25h** (**PM-109: the Background Audio body was a stub, and the row only opened from part of itself.** Reported with a picture -- "restore the background audio body, it stop working now" -- and NOT caused by the folder-session rail (proven by taking the rail off: the tile stayed 134px). An audio row asks for the full width, but how many share a line is `toColumnCount(panel width, the SHARED thumbnail slider)`, so a wider split or a smaller slider put two on a line; under ~250px Chromium drops the scrubber, the clock and the volume from an `<audio controls>` and leaves a play button. Pinned to one column, and the click now finds the ROW with `closest` instead of walking up one parent -- the name line opened nothing before. Verified live 2026-09-25: full-width player, opens from anywhere on the row.)

Previous: **matrixVersion: 2026-09-25g** (**PM-144, PM-145: every background media tab keeps FOLDER SESSIONS, on ONE short rail.** Asked for directly, from the foreground Image Show widget that already had them -- a church keeps this Sunday's pictures on a stick and its standing set in the data folder, and reaching either meant re-pointing the ONE folder Path Settings names. Images, Videos, Webs and Audios now carry the same `Default / +` strip, each session owning its own folder, view mode, sort and slide show; the Default session keeps writing the very keys the tab always used, so nothing an existing install has set moves. The strip and the slide show share one 20px row (the foreground rail came down to the same height), which a 200px panel feels as most of a row of pictures. The strip is ABOVE the file list rather than inside its body: an empty session is exactly when the way back to another one has to be on screen. Verified live 2026-09-25 on the presenter.)

Previous: **matrixVersion: 2026-09-25f** (**ED-48: a canvas box casts a shadow, and there are two kinds.** Asked for directly. **Box Shadow** is the shadow of the RECTANGLE, rounded corners included -- right for a text box with a backing colour. **Drop Shadow** is `filter: drop-shadow()`, which follows what is actually PAINTED: the letters of a box with no backing, the cut-out of a logo PNG. Handing a transparent logo a box shadow draws a rectangle in mid-air behind it, which is why this is a picker and not a checkbox. It lives in `genShapeBoxStyle`, unlike the blend, so the editor canvas, the slide thumbnails, the projector and the print PDF all agree. **No Shadow** stores nothing at all. One row added.)

Previous: **matrixVersion: 2026-09-25e** (**PM-140: the Webs background list runs a slide show too, and its tiles mark the page that is up.** Asked for directly. This tab could not borrow the Images/Videos walk: half its tiles are saved URLs rather than files, and both kinds are grouped by colour note together, so it walks an order of its own (`genBackgroundWebDisplayedSrcList`) and the show steps URL items as readily as files. Its file tiles carried the same stale badge PM-139 fixes, for the same reason and through the same marker; its URL tiles never did, not being memoised. The strip is drawn only while a web page is on a screen, and that decision moved out of CSS: a wrapper that stays in the tree keeps its row whatever it holds, so the card now keeps the strip out of the tree entirely. One row.)

Previous: **matrixVersion: 2026-09-25d** (**PM-137..PM-139: one slide-show strip, its rules opened in place, and a grid that marks what is actually up.** The control is the same compact segmented strip on all three surfaces -- the slides previewer, the background lists and the foreground media panels -- and the floating one stopped being a full-width band across the bottom of the previewer, which had blacked out a row of the very slides it was stepping through. Its rules open UNDER the bar rather than over the panel: Repeat All, a jumping Step, a Random Up To ceiling whose draw is written into the seconds box before each wait, and, for clips, Wait Until The Video Ends, which shows the clip's own length in whole seconds. The background strip is drawn only while that list has something on a screen, since a show cannot start from nothing. And the tile marking was wrong wherever it mattered: a memoised tile reads "am I on a screen?" from the managers, which no prop carried, so the item now showing stayed unmarked and the one before it kept its highlight until something remounted the list. Three rows.)

Previous: **matrixVersion: 2026-09-25c** (**PM-134..PM-136: Messages is a session of message editors, and Mask.** Alert and Announcements shipped as two widgets, were merged on sight (side by side they were the same panel showing the same thing in the same place), and the merged one then turned out to be a single text box where a message could not span lines. It is now ONE session holding SEVERAL editors: each editor is a multi-line message with its own Show / move / remove, several can be on a screen at once, and **[en:tran:Show All Messages]** puts the whole session up — as one block, or one message at a time with **[en:tran:Rotate]**. Two things only the live screen showed: two messages rendered in the SAME box until they were laid out by the LINES above them, and a multi-line message rendered only its first line until the renderer learned that `textList` is entries when rotating and lines when not. Every per-message control carries its number, because three unnumbered ones give a screen reader and `owa_click` one name three times. The mask is unchanged: static percentage bars pinned above every layer, which `Clear All` deliberately does not remove. Three rows.)

Previous: **matrixVersion: 2026-09-17g** (**RD-121 amended: a Mermaid diagram OPENS in the Mermaid Live Editor.** Asked for by the user with the copy menu's three Mermaid rows circled in a picture: _as a user I want to be able to open each copy mermaid diagram string in mermaid live editor directly, check how mermaid live share link work._ Copying a diagram is half of what a diagram is for; nothing on an ordinary machine DRAWS one but this app's own markdown preview. **Open in Mermaid Live** now sits under a divider at the foot of that menu and opens a second menu with the three Mermaid shapes. The link is the editor's own `serializeState` written out — JSON state, UTF-8, zlib deflate, URL-safe unpadded base64, `pako:` in the FRAGMENT, which never reaches a server, so nothing is uploaded — with its documented `base64:` tag as the fallback where `CompressionStream` is missing, and a measured 8 000 character ceiling past which the link is copied with a sentence instead, because `shell.openExternal` drops a longer one in silence while still resolving. 7 unit tests, the `pako` payload inflated back through Node's zlib so the encoding is proven against a decoder this app does not own. Verified live 2026-09-17 on David's graph: the row drew unclipped, Chrome opened the editor, and the same link read back through `owa_read_website` showed the editor holding this app's diagram with its Khmer names intact. A pre-existing break in this row was repaired in the same pass: a `\n` written into it had landed as a real newline and split the table row in two. No row-count change.)

Previous: **matrixVersion: 2026-09-17f** (**RD-121 amended: FIVE diagram languages on the copy menu, not one.** Asked for by the user: _add variety of diagrams, so this will let user to have more options to see many format of diagrams they want_. `GRAPH_DIAGRAM_FORMAT_LIST` declares them once — Mermaid flowchart across, Mermaid flowchart down, Mermaid mindmap, Graphviz DOT, PlantUML — and the menu, the toast and `buildGraphDiagram` all read that list, so a sixth is a row plus a branch. The mindmap needed a spanning TREE (`toChildKeyListByKey`, breadth-first and undirected from the centre, unreachable records parked on the centre) and deliberately carries no relation words. Live run also found a UI defect the first cut shipped with: a context menu in this app is 210px and CLIPS, so `Copy as Mermaid Flowchart (left to right)` and `… (top down)` both drew as `Copy as Mermaid Flowchar…` — two identical rows doing different things. Rows are named short now, with the full name on the hover (`ContextMenuItemType.title`) and on the toast. Verified live 2026-09-17 on Jacob's graph (13 children, Judah expanded): six distinct rows, and all three Mermaid shapes rendered in the app's own markdown preview. DOT and PlantUML were checked against their grammars and by unit tests only — neither `dot` nor a PlantUML renderer exists on this machine, and the app draws Mermaid only. 22 tests on the builders. No row-count change.)

Previous: **matrixVersion: 2026-09-17e** (**RD-121 amended: the Markdown copy carries the diagram in a `mermaid` fence.** Asked for by the user right after the first cut: _the markdown should include mermaid `mermaid ... ` for the diagram_. `buildGraphMarkdown` now calls `buildGraphMermaid` and opens the document with a `## Diagram` section holding it fenced, ahead of the tables — a document about a graph should show the graph, and everywhere markdown is actually rendered that block draws the same boxes the canvas has. Two guards: the fence grows to four backticks or more past any run inside the diagram (a record label carrying ``` would otherwise end the block and spill the rest into the page as prose), and a graph with no records writes no diagram at all rather than fencing a `flowchart` that declares nothing, which is a parse error wherever it lands. **Copy as Mermaid Diagram** is kept and is now the narrower job: the drawing alone, for a tool that wants only that. 14 tests on the two builders; verified live 2026-09-17 — David's 38-box graph copied as ~12.5KB and drew heading, summary, diagram, then tables in the app's own markdown preview. No row-count change.)

Previous: **matrixVersion: 2026-09-17d** (**new RD-121: the connection graph copies as Markdown or as a Mermaid diagram — and the app’s clipboard was broken.** Asked for by the user with the spot circled in a picture: _in name/location-name lookup graph preview, I want a copy icon, when click the icon it show contextmenu of `Copy as Markdown` and `Copy as Mermaid Diagram`, then implement those 2 copy format for me. for Mermaid, chose the most proper one for me._ One pure serializer (`graphTextExportHelpers.ts`, no React/DOM/app imports) writes both off the SAME visible node and edge lists `buildGraphSvg` uses. Markdown: a records table with the centre marked, connections grouped by relation with the gendered word, references capped at 12 a record. Mermaid: `flowchart LR` — the only diagram kind that carries this graph whole (arrows where a relation has two different ends, plain lines where not, a label on every line, arbitrary cross-links; a `mindmap` cannot link two branches, an `erDiagram` describes kinds rather than records) — with a `classDef` per record kind carrying the canvas’s own accent as a stroke. Two choices came out of the LIVE run rather than the design: references are capped (19KB → 7.6KB for David’s 29 boxes; Solomon alone cites 174) and the direction is `LR` (the same graph as `TD` renders as one unreadable row 28 boxes wide). **The verification also found the feature’s own blocker, an app-wide bug**: Electron exposes `clipboard` to the MAIN process only, so `systemUtils.copyToClipboard` in the renderer threw `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'writeText')` and every Copy in the app answered **Reload is needed**; it now sends `main:app:copy-to-clipboard` and main writes the clipboard. 11 unit tests on the two builders; verified live 2026-09-17 on the dev reader, both formats pasted into a `.md` and rendered in the app’s own markdown preview. Total 830 → **831**.)

Previous: **matrixVersion: 2026-09-17c** (**new RD-120: files can be copied INTO a Resources folder; RD-87 amended.** Asked for by the user with a picture of a group's menu circled: _as a user I want to be able to copy one or more files to the resources selected folder… in `Resource` for contextmenu of selected folder add `Add Files` to select files to copy to the folder._ A group's menu gains **Add Files** (`bi-file-earmark-plus`) under **Add Folder**, opening the multi-select picker; `copyFilesIntoResourcesFolder` then copies each picked file into that folder one at a time (sequential, `fs.copyFile`, the sources untouched), taking the next free name (`genFreeFilePath`, the index BEFORE the extension) rather than overwriting, passing over a path that is already that file here or is gone, and on a disk error sweeping up the part file and stopping with what already landed. The box invalidates its own cached walk, re-scans and opens if it was folded, and the toast counts what landed and what did not — plus, when nothing copied will be DRAWN (named after no open chapter, **Others** unticked), one sentence saying to tick **Others**, since a shelf that does not visibly change is indistinguishable from a copy that failed. Unit-tested on the real disk (the copy, a taken name, a file already there, a gone path, a folder, a refusal, a failure half way) and the wording and the `isNoneListed` handoff tested in the box. Verified live 2026-09-17 on the dev reader over CDP: the item sits between **Add Folder** and **Reveal in File Explorer** on the `Document` group; a `GEN.1.claude-check.txt` picked through the real dialog appeared under `GEN.1.*` without a refresh, the same file picked again landed as `GEN.1.claude-check (1).txt` with the toast **Add Files — 1 file copied** and the first copy untouched, and both were deleted and the group refreshed. Total 829 → **830**.)

Previous: **matrixVersion: 2026-09-16a** (**new RD-117: a Resources folder can be copied into the data folder; RD-87 amended.** Asked for by the user with a picture of a Resources group's menu, **Reveal in File Explorer** underlined: _move selected folder in Resources to under selected-dir so I can manage it easily_, then _after copied then change the selection to the copied one_. The group menu gains **Copy to Data Directory** (`bi-copy`) between Reveal and Remove Folder, left out for a folder already under `<parent dir>/resources`. It confirms with the source path and the destination, copies the tree one entry at a time (`fs.copyFile`, links skipped) under a hidden `.copying-<ms>-<name>` staging folder renamed into place at the end, and replaces the group IN PLACE in `resources-folder-list`, carrying its open/collapsed setting to the copy and deleting the original's. A folder holding the parent dir (a `Desktop` group above a data folder that lives on that Desktop) is refused before anything is written. Measured from inside a live guest on claude.ai: the site could not READ anything on this computer — CORS refused the app's CDP door, `host.mjs`'s Origin check refused its MCP door, Chromium's own origin rule refused a CDP WebSocket — but a blind `no-cors` fetch at BOTH doors went out and was served, and the same request reaches the church's router, NAS and printers. The guest session now cancels every request to a local or private address, by the same `webUrlPolicy.mjs` predicate the MCP firewall uses (`checkIsLocalHostname`, added there and now the one implementation `checkWebUrl` uses too); after it, both doors, `127.1`, `2130706433`, `0x7f.1`, `127.0.0.2`, `[::1]`, `192.168.1.1`, `169.254.169.254` and `printer` are all refused and the site's own origin still answers 200 — the positive control matters, a wall that blocks the site is a brick. Beside it, `AC-01`: the persistent partition is a credential store, and closing every tab never touched it, so **Sign out of every site** is now a **↤** in the head row and a line on the chooser card, asking first with _Keep me signed in_ focused, clearing the tabs' remembered pages and site-given names while keeping a name the user typed. `probe-aichat.mjs` 22 → **33 checks, all held**. The chord is now written WHERE IT LANDS, as `|[D]` with the bar OUTSIDE the brackets -- `[|D]` is what the page looks like and it is refused by open-lyric and by our own validator alike, both probed before the form was chosen and the probe kept as a test -- and bounded three ways so it cannot eat a leading word that happens to be a chord. Every renderer runs with `nodeIntegration: true`, so `evaluate_script` over the MCP host was arbitrary code execution on the operator's machine — proven live, `require('os').userInfo()` and `require('fs').readFileSync(setting.json)`, from a script with no credential — and that tool was sent to the chatbot's model on every round, where an attachment somebody handed the user could reach it. `firewall.mjs` now sits on the one seam both doors share: three tools denied AND dropped from `tools/list` (47 → 44, ~668 tokens/round), navigation allowlisted to pages the app serves, a **point-don't-press** interlock on labels that cannot be undone, an acting-call rate limit, and provider keys scrubbed out of every result. Previous: **matrixVersion: 2026-09-02b** (**new CB-36: the app now has an assistant before anybody has an API key.** Asked for from `awesome-free-llm-apis`: _"is there any api we can use ... when user have no api keys set we should provide chatbot access as well"_, then _"show warning when using free one, let user aware of risk"_. Of 17 free providers only three answer keyless and only two can call a tool, which is the one thing this bot cannot work without; both are wired as one `Free` provider that sorts LAST so any real key still outranks it. Graded first against the standing corpus through the real 44-tool loop — 7/8 answered, 0 internals leaked — which is what sized the free-only round cap and found three defects a paid API never produces. The trade is stated in a sticky notice above the log and in Settings, never made quietly. Total 799 → **800**.)

Previous: **matrixVersion: 2026-09-02a** (**new CB-35: a picture with an empty box is a question, not a malformed request.** Reported from the window with the transcript: the assistant asked for a screenshot, the user sent one with nothing typed, and the provider refused the request outright because only a file or a pointed-at control contributes words — so the ask arrived as an empty text block. The refusal was then shown as an unreachable provider, with the offline bot's generic greeting under it. One decision point now says what the model is asked, the loop refuses to post an empty ask at all, and the offline half degrades honestly. Total 798 → **799**.)

Previous: **matrixVersion: 2026-09-01m** (**new CB-33, CB-34 and PC-33: the assistant and the annotation overlay belong to every window now.** Asked for from the app: _"add chatbot assistant and presenting-control to all pages except about.html, chatbot.html, finder.html, screen.html"_, then _"have to extend the list to support all question files"_. One component mounts both on all nine pages; the way in everywhere is **Tools → Start Controlling** / **Ctrl+Shift+P** and **Tools → App Assistant** / **Ctrl+Shift+A**, since only three windows have a top bar to hold a button. The menu click now routes to the FOCUSED window — one entry is kept per menu key, so the last window to load owned it and opening Settings quietly took _Start Controlling_ away from the presenter. **ASKING ABOUT** grew from two names to eight, declared once in `botFocus.mjs` and read by the picker, the two MCP tool schemas, the manual's focus filter and the session validator alike; the corpus grew `bible-note`, `web-editor` and `lyric-editor`, and the Slide Editor's own questions were split out of the Presenter's. CB-01 rewritten. Total 795 → **798**.)
Previous: **matrixVersion: 2026-09-01l** (**new CB-32: the ask box holds several lines, and the help window can report a bug for you.** Asked for from the app with a screenshot of the ask row: _"change input text to textarea to support multiple lines"_, then _"under `Ask` add `Report`"_ — the agent to investigate first, collect the evidence and prepare it for an issue tracker — then _"ctrl+enter to ask, for normal enter just make new line"_ and _"to prevent click REPORT by accident, should confirm before running report"_. The box is a growing textarea; **Report** sits under **Ask**, asks before it runs, photographs the app, reads build/window/screens/console for itself, has the model investigate the live app, and prepares a document nothing sends until a second press. There is no issue tracker endpoint yet and the window says so rather than pretending: it saves the report and the picture into Downloads. Total 794 → **795**.)

Previous: **matrixVersion: 2026-09-01k** (**new CB-26..CB-30: the ask box takes more than words, and an answer on its way can be added to.** Asked for from the app: attach files and images, paste an image, point at a DOM element, take a screenshot — and, mid-turn, _"during waiting for api response user should able to add more input"_ and _"for something unclear the ai should ask for more input from user"_. Five ways in (paperclip, paste, drop, **📷**, **🎯**), all landing on one capped list of chips; the picture is held in memory for the life of the window and NEVER written to `chatbot-sessions`, which the app reads whole at startup — a reopened tab shows the chip greyed rather than a settings file with a screenshot in it. Pointing swallows the choosing click in the capture phase, so asking what **Clear Bible** does never clears the bible, and answers with a unique selector tested against the document before it is returned. The box is no longer disabled while an answer comes: **Add** folds what you type into the answer being written, a **Stop** puts every added word back in the box, and anything that arrives too late to fold is asked on its own and says so. The assistant can ask to be SHOWN — a `NEEDS:` frame the code strips unconditionally, rendered as the same buttons. The Presenting Control gains a **📷** that photographs the app with the drawing on it, offering ask / copy / save-into-images, over the one capture IPC that also serves the new `owa_screenshot`. Two tools added to the server and NEITHER offered to the chatbot's model, so a volunteer's question costs the same tokens per round as before. Total 788 → **794**.)

Previous: **matrixVersion: 2026-09-01j** (**CB-02, CB-08 and CB-12 amended: every head-row drop-down says what it is FOR, not only what it is set to.** Reported from the app with a screenshot circling the pair — the head row read `Presenter | ChatGPT`, two words with nothing to say which was the half of the app and which the service answering about it. The only explanation was a `title` hover, which is not a thing a volunteer goes looking for, and an `aria-label` no sighted user ever meets. Each control now wears a visible caption — **ASKING ABOUT**, **ASSISTANT**, **MODEL**, and **ANSWERS FROM** over the offline button — beside it, as a real `<label>` wrapping the control, so the pair reads as a line and the caption is a second click target for the control it names. Below 560px, the width this window opens at, the caption moves over its control instead: three captions written beside three controls is 463px of a 436px row, and the thing that would be pushed off the end is the model name. Verified live 2026-09-01 at both widths. No `aria-label` moved and no class was renamed, so `extra-work/verify-chatbot-e2e.mjs`, which finds all three by `.chat-head-row select[aria-label]`, is untouched. Total 788.)

Previous: **matrixVersion: 2026-09-01i** (**new CB-24 and CB-25: the answer, and the walkthrough under it, are about the question that was asked.** Reported from the app with a screenshot and in the user's own words -- _"get many wrong answers. the assistant help with unrelevant things"_. The presenter's own starter chip **"Is any screen showing right now?"** was answered correctly and then followed by an eight-step walkthrough of **Show the keys you press (Keyboard Screencast)**. Three independent defects. `owa_help_search` matched a term of four letters or more against the START of any longer word with no bound on the rest, so **"screen" matched "Screencast"** in a page TITLE, worth 14 -- 45 such pairs are live in this corpus (`copy`->`copyright`, `song`->`SongSelect`, `back`->`background`, `down`->`download`, `stop`->`stopwatch`), 229 occurrences, 10 of them in a title; the tail is now capped at three characters, and coverage is weighted by inverse frequency rather than counting words, and no longer squared. The two walkthrough buttons under an answer carried the top manual hit of the model's FIRST search and could never be revised -- not by a refined query, not by the page it actually opened with `owa_help_page`, not by it answering from `owa_list_screens`; a page the model OPENED now wins, a later search overwrites an earlier one, and a model that put its own card up is offered no button. And four supported questions named a recipe, `W-01b`, that no manual page carried: `build-manual.mjs` matched `W-\d+` only, so that heading was silently folded into W-01's page and never written, which `questions.test.mjs` could not catch because it checked the recipe id's SHAPE and called that "a real manual id". Graded on the 236-question corpus as a labelled retrieval set -- which nothing had ever done -- top-1 136 -> **140**, top-3 179 -> **186**, and 45 held-out volunteer paraphrases 21 -> **23**; per query, 9 fixed and 3 broken. **41% of supported questions still miss their own recipe**, filed as `EC-50` -- the reason rung 2 is still not marked reached. Total 786 -> **788**.)

Previous: **matrixVersion: 2026-09-01h** (**new CB-23: an answer on its way can be stopped.** Reported from the app with a screenshot of `Looking it up…` and no way back -- the box disabled, **Ask** disabled, and a question asked by mistake could only be waited out or the window closed. A question is up to ten model rounds and is paid for the whole way. **Ask** becomes **Stop** while an answer is coming, **Esc** does the same, and both ABORT the request rather than ignore its result -- verified live 2026-09-01 with ChatGPT, `net::ERR_ABORTED` on the round in flight, no late answer, and the happy path unchanged. A stop is never described as a service failure and never falls through to the offline bot. The row count also picks up CB-22, which was added without it. Total 784 -> **786**.)

Previous: **matrixVersion: 2026-09-01g** (**CB-06, CB-08 and CB-12 rewritten, plus a new CB-22: a THIRD provider, Kimi (Moonshot), answers in the chatbot, and every AI key row now says what its key is for.** Kimi speaks OpenAI's protocol, so the OpenAI tool loop was parameterised rather than cloned -- one `askOpenAiCompatible` plus a per-provider descriptor -- and the provider set is now declared once in `LLM_PROVIDER_MAP` with `Record<LlmProviderType, ...>` dispatch, replacing three two-way ternaries that each sent an unrecognised provider to OpenAI in silence. Kimi's budget rule is its own: every model offered thinks, so all get the 6000-token budget, and `reasoning_effort` goes only to `kimi-k3`. Verified live 2026-09-01 on a real key: `kimi-k3` and `kimi-k2.6` both answered in steps, **More models...** pulled `kimi-k2.7-code` off the account, and a bad model id fell back to the manual reading _"Kimi could not answer"_. Also fixed a latent data-loss bug in `setAISetting`, which rebuilt the secret blob from a hand-listed pair of fields: a Kimi-only key was deleted by the very save that stored it. Total 784 -> **785**.)

Previous: **matrixVersion: 2026-09-01f** (**CB-02 and CB-08 rewritten: both head-row switches are drop-downs.** They were segmented pairs of buttons beside a model picker that was already a `<select>`; six uppercase words spent most of a 460px window on two either/or choices and pushed the model name into an ellipsis. Both are `<select>`s now, the disabled provider says **needs an API key** in the option itself rather than on a hover nobody sees, and the provider picker's `aria-label` moved to **Which assistant answers** because it used to share the model picker's. `extra-work/verify-chatbot-e2e.mjs` drives them by option, not by click.)

Answers only ever carried buttons when the model happened to read a manual page; anything answered from live app state carried nothing but **Copy**. ## Mandatory core — screen controlling, presenting, locale, and media download (every run)

Three blocks are **never optional**: every run — full-coverage OR focused (e.g. "robot test
bible lookup") — must exercise the **mandatory core** and record its rows in the run
state file.

**1. Screen controlling & presenting** — the app's reason to exist:

> **SP-01, SP-02, SC-01, SC-02, PR-04, KB-05 (or another clear key)** — present at
> least one real content item, verify it on the mini-screen AND on the `screen.html`
> CDP target while showing, exercise the clear controls, then hide/restore.

**2. Locale switch** — the bug class a single-locale run cannot see:

> **LT-01, LT-02** — re-walk the screens the run touched in the OTHER language, assert
> no `Translation for text "…" not found in locale km-KH` console error and no blank
> panel, then restore the starting locale.

`tran()` returns early when the locale is `en-US` (`DEFAULT_LOCALE`) — it never looks a
key up. In Khmer the same call **throws** on a missing key, and with no error boundary
the subtree renders **blank**. So an English-only pass proves nothing about translation
coverage, and typecheck/tests/build all stay green while a screen is broken in Khmer.

**3. Media download (video + audio)** — the one flow that runs external binaries:

> **MD-05, MD-01, MD-02, MD-04** — install the media pack if it is absent, download a
> video AND an audio from the canonical test link (below) through the Background panel,
> then **delete both again**. Nothing else in the app spawns yt-dlp / ffmpeg / qjs, so a
> broken or missing binary is invisible to every other row and to typecheck/tests/build
> alike — and nothing else in the run writes ~100 MB per pass into the user's data dir, so
> the block that creates them owns removing them (MD-04). A run that downloads without
> cleaning up is **incomplete**.
>
> The binaries are no longer inside the app: they are installed from **Settings → Others →
> Extra Binaries** into `<data parent>/extra-bin/` (MD-05), and a download attempted
> without them raises a confirm dialog rather than failing (MD-06). Do NOT delete
> `extra-bin` as part of teardown — unlike the downloaded media, it is not this run's
> garbage, and re-installing it costs ~27 MB every pass.

**Canonical test link** (use this one so runs are comparable):

```
https://youtu.be/ZSsOrph7rJs?list=RDZSsOrph7rJs
```

A report that lacks evidence for any of the three blocks is **incomplete** — say so
explicitly rather than shipping it. Full recipes: test-plan.md §S7 (screen), §S15
(locale) and §S19 (media download).

## Presenting Flow deep mode — a focused run with its own row contract

The argument `presentingFlow` (or `run sheet`) is **not a focus area that trims the run**; it
selects a tracked MODE (SKILL.md §6f, recipe test-plan §S20, model knowledge-base §14)
with coverage accounting ON and this exact scope set:

> **PL-10, PL-29, PL-32..PL-76, PL-81..PL-102 = 69 rows**, every one ending the run with a
> status in `coverage-<runid>.json` (`"focus": "presentingFlow"`).
>
> Plus the **mandatory core** (SP/SC/LT/MD), ridden from the presenting flow itself — present a
> row and drive its `screen.html` target.
>
> Plus, when the run touches them: **PL-77..PL-80** and **NAV-17/18** (the `.owadoc` /
> `.owadata` archives share the presenting flow bundle's code) and **XW-01..07** (a document
> edited in another window must reach the sheet's rows).
>
> **Out of scope in this mode:** PL-01..PL-09, PL-11..PL-28, PL-30/31 — the
> Documents/Lyrics lists and the generic file-list chrome — except where the fixture uses
> them.

The mode's coverage denominator is therefore `69 − EXCLUDED`, reported separately from a
full run's 651. The rows most easily claimed without evidence are called out in the report
template: the **13 screen actions fired against a showing screen** (PL-72/74), the
**folded-sheet walk** (PL-99) and the **performance measurements** (PL-63/70).

## How a run uses this matrix

1. This file is the **static inventory** — never write statuses into it.
2. Track statuses in a per-run state file
   `test-results/robot-test/coverage-<runid>.json` (schema in SKILL.md §"Coverage
   accounting"). Update it after every few rows so an interrupted run can resume.
3. Statuses:
   - **PASS** — interaction performed, expected observable confirmed, evidence recorded.
   - **FAIL** — interaction performed, expectation not met → also file a Finding.
   - **PARTIAL** — some interactions of the row done, others not (say which in `note`).
   - **BLOCKED** — could not exercise; `note` must say why (e.g. "no camera device").
   - **EXCLUDED** — matches a policy exclusion (EX-xx); `note` names the EX id.
4. **Evidence rule:** a row only counts as PASS/FAIL with at least one of: a screenshot
   path, an `evaluate_script` assertion result, or a console/network diff. "I clicked it
   and nothing crashed" without a checked observable = PARTIAL at best.
5. **Coverage formula** (goes in the report):

   ```
   in-scope   = total rows − EXCLUDED
   exercised  = PASS + FAIL
   coverage % = exercised / in-scope × 100
   ```

   Target for a full run: **100% of in-scope rows attempted; ≥ 99% exercised**, with
   every BLOCKED/PARTIAL row listed with its reason. Never inflate the number — an
   honest 97% with reasons beats a fake 100%.

## Policy exclusions (EX)

These are out of scope **by policy**, not laziness. They count separately and never
against coverage. Where a "covered-to-the-edge" trick exists, use it — it converts the
row's control to exercisable while excluding only the un-drivable/destructive tail.

| ID    | Excluded                                                                                               | Why                                          | Cover to the edge by…                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| ----- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| EX-01 | OS-native file dialogs (browse/open/save)                                                              | Not drivable via CDP                         | click the button, confirm the app doesn't crash while the dialog is cancelled by policy — mark the _dialog itself_ excluded                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| EX-02 | **Leaving** the user's real display taken over, or OS-fullscreen during a live service                 | The user may be actively presenting (KB §10) | **Showing the screen is now MANDATORY, not excluded** (SP-01/SC-01): toggle it on briefly, drive the `screen.html` CDP target, then hide + restore. EX-02 applies only to _leaving_ it showing, or when the user explicitly said the display is in live use — then assert via mini-screen only and mark the SC rows BLOCKED→EX-02 |
| EX-03 | Camera-dependent rows                                                                                  | Needs hardware; may be absent                | if a device exists, exercise; else BLOCKED→EX-03                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| EX-04 | Following external links (Help, About links)                                                           | Opens the user's browser                     | click-eligibility only: control present, named, enabled                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| EX-05 | Destructive tails: `Clear All Settings`, `Reset All Child Directories`, deleting user documents/lyrics | Destroys user data/state                     | click → **confirm dialog appears → Cancel** (covers the control + dialog); for delete, create a scratch item first, delete _that_. **`Reset Widgets Size` is NOT on this list any more** — it moved to View (NAV-21), only touches pane sizes, and is undone by re-dragging, so that row is taken all the way through **Yes**     |
| EX-06 | App quit / relaunch flows                                                                              | Kills the session under test                 | —                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| EX-07 | Downloading new bible versions                                                                         | Large network payloads on the user's machine | verify list/search/enable-disable UI; toggle an already-downloaded version and restore                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |

Nothing arms it from ROW hover: that reached only some hosts, and a touch screen hovers nothing. **Geometry is the shared class's, never the host's**: one `22×22px` box (`--app-action-rail`) everywhere, and in a list it sits in the row's **action rail** — `.app-action-rail--pinned` against the row's border edge (so one inset whatever the row's own padding is), stretched but capped at `--app-action-rail-line` (34px) so it centres on a leaf row EXACTLY and stays up on the header line of a row that holds other rows. Measurable: across the reader's Bibles + Bible Notes + Resources panels every ⋮ reads one inset, one box, and `dy ≤ 2px` from its own line's centre — before the rail they measured three insets (0/2/5px), two boxes (18×24 and 18×17) and a file row's ⋮ parked 130px down its own children, level with one of THEIRS. Rows carrying a pinned rail hold its width open (`.app-has-action-rail`, `-2` for a two-slot rail) so a long title ellipsizes at the rail instead of running under it. Two wirings, and the difference is testable: with an `onOpening` it calls that handler; WITHOUT one it dispatches a real `contextmenu` on its parent, so a capturing ancestor still wins — the `⋮` on a slide card inside a presenting flow's preview must open the RUN's menu (park/pin/CC), not the slide's own (src: src/context-menu/ContextMenuDotsButtonComp.tsx:23) |

Next cycles in catalog order. All tips opens every current-page lesson with purpose, topic and a live filtered/total count; a no-match search has a translated empty state. Presenter exposes exactly 61 lessons and every checked-in Presenter demo id appears exactly once: 51 lessons begin with a safe deterministic Do it for a visible control or shortcut; ten native-menu lessons remain self-guided. Mixed lessons advance from their safe action to explanation-only `look` steps rendered as Next, never a dead Do it. Reader exposes exactly 54 lessons and every checked-in Reader demo id appears exactly once. Both catalogs have searchable File, Edit, Tools, Window, and Help overviews that name every visible, conditional, and macOS-only row; their seven detailed View lessons cover every View command. On both pages, disruptive Reload/Relaunch/Developer Tools lessons remain searchable but never enter the random daily pool. Choosing a lesson returns to its card. Show it starts the matching checked-in `owa_guide_start { demoId }` card without a model/provider call; if a hot-reloaded renderer is ahead of its long-running MCP host, an unknown or stale show-only built-in is retried with the current inline lesson. No lesson auto-presents, reloads, relaunches, exports, resets layout, or opens Developer Tools. With AI features off it offers Settings → Others. Don't show again disables future automatic tips globally, but either translated Help item can always reopen one suggestion or the complete library without re-enabling automatic tips. The General setting reflects that disabled state; turning it on restores automatic tips for both pages on the next app launch without clearing any other setting. Close, reload and switching pages do not create another automatic tip in that launch (src: src/toast/DailyTipComp.tsx, `dailyTipHelpers.ts`, `dailyTipSettingHelpers.ts`, src/setting/SettingGeneralOtherOptionsComp.tsx, tools/owa-devtools-mcp/appMenuDemos.mjs, tools/owa-devtools-mcp/readerDemos.mjs, tools/owa-devtools-mcp/presenterDemos.mjs, W-46) |

least one kind per run; the code path is identical for the others (`.owapf` / `.owadoc` /
`.owbible` / `.owabn` / `.owadata`).

The data archive shows the same fields below its folder list, under a separator — ONE dialog, not two (src: src/popup-widget/ArchivePasswordComp.tsx, src/setting/data-archive/dataArchiveMenuHelpers.tsx:59)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |

This is the regression that matters most: protection is OPTIONAL and the default path must not change (src: src/helper/archiveNameHelpers.ts `toArchiveDotExtension`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| AP-03 | Password ⇒ `.enc` bundle          | type the same password in both fields, **Ok**                                                      | writes `<name>.<kind>.enc` instead. First 7 bytes are `OWAENC\0`, byte 7 is the container version `01`, byte 8 the KDF id `01`, byte 9 `0f` (scrypt log2 N = 15), byte 10 `08` (r), byte 11 `01` (p). `tar` refuses it ("not in gzip format"). No `.part` file is left in Downloads (src: electron/archiveCryptoHelpers.ts)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| AP-04 | Mismatched confirmation           | type different values in the two fields                                                            | the dialog says **Passwords do not match** live, and **Ok** re-asks instead of exporting — **inline, with NO intermediate alert popup**, on all five kinds. Press **Ok** a SECOND time without changing anything: it must re-ask AGAIN, still **holding both typed values** and — on the two one-dialog flows (Export Data, Export Bible Data) — **the operator's item selection**. An alert between the two `showAppInput` calls unmounts the popup and blanks both, after which one more Ok exported the whole list UNPROTECTED. Three tries, then the export is abandoned. Also: clearing BOTH fields settles the complaint (empty is the legitimate "no password"), and a value typed into **Confirm Password** alone is flagged rather than silently exported unprotected (src: src/popup-widget/ArchivePasswordComp.tsx `MAX_PASSWORD_ATTEMPTS`, src/setting/data-archive/dataArchiveMenuHelpers.tsx `askForFolders`, src/setting/bible-setting/bibleXMLArchiveMenuHelpers.tsx `askForBibles`; regression tests `tells a NEW listener the values it is already holding`, `tells a NEW listener the selection it is already holding`, `drops the re-ask complaint once both fields are cleared`, `flags a confirmation typed against an empty password`) |
| AP-05 | Import asks for the password      | drag a `.enc` bundle onto its list, or `globalThis.tryDataImport('<path>')`                        | the drop gate ACCEPTS the `.enc` name (it must not fall through to "copy into the folder"), then a one-field dialog says **This archive is password protected**. The right password imports normally — for a presenting flow, under the ORIGINAL archive's base name, never the temp file's (src: src/helper/archivePasswordHelpers.ts `openArchiveForReading`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| AP-06 | Wrong password, retry, give up    | submit a wrong password                                                                            | rejects in well under a second even on a gigabyte archive (the container's key check answers before any payload is read), re-asks with **Wrong password, try again**, allows three tries in total, then reports failure under the flow's own title. Cancel at the prompt aborts silently with no toast (src: src/helper/archivePasswordHelpers.ts)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| AP-07 | A plain bundle is never prompted  | drag an ordinary `.tar.gz` bundle onto its list                                                    | imports with NO password dialog at all. Detection is by the container magic, not the name — so a plain bundle someone renamed to `.enc` also imports silently, and a `.enc` renamed to something else still asks (src: src/server/appHelpers.ts `checkIsEncryptedFile`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| AP-08 | The dialog in Khmer               | switch the app to Khmer, then repeat AP-01 and AP-05                                               | title, both field labels, the reveal toggle, the hint, the mismatch line and the retry line all render in Khmer and the page does NOT blank. `tran()` throws on a missing key in dev, so an English-only pass structurally cannot see a gap here (keys guarded by src/lang/data/km/index.test.ts)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |

## PL — Presenter, left column

> Two subsystems share this prefix. **PL-01..PL-09 / PL-11..PL-28 / PL-30..PL-31** are the
> Documents & Lyrics lists and the generic file-list chrome. **PL-10, PL-29, PL-32..PL-76,
> PL-81..PL-102** are the **run sheet** — the 69-row scope set of presenting flow deep mode
> (§"Presenting Flow deep mode" above); their model is knowledge-base §14, their recipe
> test-plan §S20.

| PL-95  | **Run actions** — `Next: Interval` / `Next: Timeout`                                                                                          | 🖱️R a presenting flow → **Add Action** → **Next: Timeout**, answer **5** (and Cancel the question once); repeat with **Next: Interval** / **3**; 🖱️R each new row; open the floating preview and 🖱️ the timeout element, then let it run out; arm it again and press any key mid-count; arm the interval and click/press keys while it counts, then 🖱️ the ⊗ pill; put an interval directly above a timeout and let it hand over; then 🖱️R a SLIDE row → **Add CC Elements** and read the list; attach the timeout, open the preview and step onto that slide with the next-key; 🖱️R the CC row; then 🖱️R the timeout row → **Change Timing**, switch the chooser to **At Time**, set a time a couple of minutes ahead and 🖱️ the row; repeat with a time that has already gone by; finally CLOSE the preview and 🖱️ a run-action row in the tree | the question is asked BEFORE the entry exists, so **Cancel adds nothing**; the row then reads `⏱ Next: Timeout (5)` / `⟳ Next: Interval (3)` — the number is part of the label in both the tree and the preview's button, and **Change Seconds** (the row's own menu entry, opening on its current value) re-arms it in place. **A TIMEOUT may be armed with a TIME OF DAY instead**: its question's left half is a `Seconds` / `At Time` chooser (the interval's stays a plain `Seconds` label), the time field opens FIVE MINUTES ahead of now when there is no time to open on, the row then reads `⏱ Next: Timeout (7:05 AM)` — 12-hour with AM/PM, from the stored 24-hour `HH:mm`, never the system's own format — and its menu entry says **Change Timing**, re-opening on the half it was armed with. The two are alternatives, never both: re-arming with one DELETES the other. Firing it counts to that time TODAY (the pill reads `m:ss` / `h:mm:ss`, not a five-digit second count), and the remainder is re-read from the wall clock each tick, so a laptop that sleeps mid-count still fires on time. A time that has already gone by is **refused**, with the toast **The set time is already due** titled **Next: Timeout** — it is never rolled over to tomorrow, and nothing is armed. A run action reaches NO screen: its menu is **Start Auto Next** + **Change Seconds** and nothing else — no **Reveal Original**, no **Apply on Screens**, no **Set Specific Screen**, no **Add CC Elements** — it is not draggable onto a mini screen, and it never appears in another row's **Add CC Elements** list. In the preview a warning-coloured pill appears at the widget's top-right showing the seconds left: a TIMEOUT counts down once, forces the next selection at 0 (the cursor moves on, and what it lands on fires exactly as the next-key fires it) and is then spent. **Only the RUN MOVING touches either clock** — the preview's cursor changing to another element or to another slide of the one it is on. That CANCELS a timeout and RESTARTS an interval's count from full; a click on a background, a button, the widget's own chrome, or any keypress that does not move the run, leaves both alone (an unintended click killing the wait was the first design and is a bug). Arming is never cancelled by the gesture that armed it, and tidying the sheet — a reorder that shifts the element the run is on — must not cancel it either. An interval is otherwise ended only by the pill, by closing the widget, or by the end of the sheet. An auto-step that lands on another run action hands the clock over to it. With the preview closed — or open on ANOTHER presenting flow — triggering one toasts **Open the presenting flow preview to use this action** and nothing else happens. **A TIMEOUT may be a CC element and an INTERVAL may not**: the timeout appears in every row's **Add CC Elements** list (its seconds in the label) and the interval never does, so a slide can carry "go on by yourself N seconds later" while nothing can carry a loop no input can stop. A CC'd timeout arms when its HOST reaches a screen — dismiss the "which screen?" menu and no countdown starts — and it raises no second screen question of its own. **Its CC row drops Set Specific Screen for a clock of its OWN**: a hollow `stopwatch` in the action's amber sits where the media controller's gear does, and it (or the row's **Change Timing**) opens the very same question the element's row asks, on whatever this row is counting now. The answer is stored on the ATTACHMENT (`ccItems[].actionArming`), never on the element, so ONE timeout element attached to two lines can hold one for 4s and the other for 30s; the glyph then reads **filled**, and a second entry, **Use Element Timing** (ប្រើការកំណត់ពេលរបស់ធាតុ), appears and hands the row back (glyph hollow again, key deleted). Absence still means the element's, so re-arming the element moves every follower that has none and leaves the overridden ones alone; a time of day written over seconds deletes the seconds, as on the element. A `Jump to`'s pointer never gets the glyph — it is never fired. It moves the run on from where the PREVIEW's cursor is, so a host presented from the tree while the panel sits elsewhere advances the panel, not the tree (src: src/presenting-flow/presentingFlowAutoNextHelpers.ts:1, src/presenting-flow/presentingFlowActionHelpers.ts:190, src/presenting-flow/PresentingFlowPreviewFloatingComp.tsx:106, src/presenting-flow/PresentingFlowCcRowsComp.tsx:140) |

| PL-102 | **Screen action** — `Slide: Media Control` (the media INSIDE a slide, driven from the run sheet)                                              | 🖱️R a presenting flow file row → **Add Action** and look for it; then 🖱️R a SLIDE row (or a document element) → **Add Media Control**; Cancel the panel once, then fill it in (Action **Play**, Delay Before **3**, Media Start At **10**, Then Pause **At Media Time** **70**, tick **Volume** 70, tick **Speed** 2x) and OK; read the new CC row; 🖱️ its cyan gear, and 🖱️R it; present the host slide and watch the video on the mini screen AND on the `screen.html` target; switch Action to **Pause** and to **Stop** and watch which fields disappear; pin the CC to a screen the host does NOT reach and present again; remove the element; then run the app in Khmer                                                                                                                                                                     | it is **not in the Add Action menu at all** — the only action that is not, because "start this video ten seconds in" is a sentence about ONE slide, so it is authored from the slide instead: **Add Media Control** (បន្ថែមការគ្រប់គ្រងមេឌៀ, cyan `sliders`) sits right under **Add CC Elements** on a slide row, a document element row and every slide row inside a document — and on nothing else. The panel (**Slide: Media Control - Settings**) is asked BEFORE the line exists, so **Cancel adds nothing**; OK writes the action element AND the CC that points at it in ONE go. Fields that mean nothing in the chosen mode are HIDDEN, not greyed: **Pause** drops the start point and the stop point, **Stop** drops only the stop point. **Volume** and **Speed** are behind ticks because "not set" is a real answer — an unticked volume must leave the level the operator set by hand on the mini screen alone. The CC row reads the mode then the numbers (`Slide: Media Control (Play +3s 10s→70s 70% 2x)`, translated mode, numbers appended AFTER it) and carries a cyan **gear** that reopens the panel on its stored values; **Media Control Settings** on its right-click menu is the same door. The listed ELEMENT row shows the bare label with no gear and does nothing when clicked — the settings live on the ATTACHMENT, so the same controller attached to two slides means two different things. Presenting the host then plays EVERY media in that slide: after the delay the video seeks to the start point and runs at the set speed with the set volume, pausing at the media time asked for; the projected screen follows at the SAME speed and stays muted (sound is the presenter machine's, by design), and a canvas `audio` item plays on the presenter only. A **pin narrows** rather than redirects: pinned to a screen the host also reached it runs there alone, pinned to one the host never reached it runs NOWHERE (there is no media on it to drive). **UNSELECTING the host stops what it started**: presenting another slide on that screen — or clearing it — pauses every media of the outgoing slide (native elements and YouTube alike) and drops anything still armed, so the sheet can move on. That is the whole point of it being the SHEET's media: media the operator started by clicking the mini screen still REFUSES the swap with **Media is Playing**, and must be checked both ways — with a controller armed the next slide lands silently, without one the toast still appears and the slide stays. The controller is spent with the slide it rode, so the swap after that is guarded again (src: src/presenting-flow/presentingFlowActionHelpers.ts:383, src/presenting-flow/presentingFlowMediaControlDialogHelpers.tsx:317, src/_screen/managers/screenSlideMediaControlHelpers.ts:262, src/_screen/managers/ScreenVaryAppDocumentManager.ts:207)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |

Attaching one makes **Add CC Elements** disappear (exactly one; a second is refused with **This element takes only one CC element**, and a hand-edited file with two draws only the first), and the jump can never be attached to anything itself. **The two refusals must not be confused**: a drop on a CLOCK — which accepts none — says **This element does not accept CC element**, while a second one on a jump says **This element takes only one CC element**. Firing it is the NEXT-KEY aimed at a chosen line: the cursor moves there — BACKWARDS up the sheet is the point — and whatever is there fires exactly as it would have on a step, entering a document at its FIRST slide and **arming a clock it lands on** (an interval walking a set of slides with a jump at the end of them pointing back at that interval is the looping set, and it must run without the operator). A PARKED target is passed over. The ONE thing withheld is another **Jump to** (`movesRunAtOnce`): it is selected but not fired, since two aimed at each other would move the run for ever with nothing in between. | PM-126 | `FloatingWidgetComp` maximize/restore (header double-press)                                                                                                                                                                       | 🖱️🖱️ the blank part of a TITLED widget's header, then 🖱️🖱️ it again                                                                                                                                                                                              | 1st: the widget fills the viewport (`left/top` = 8, size = viewport − 16, ignoring any `options.maxWidth/maxHeight`). 2nd: it goes back to the exact rect it had, clamped to the viewport. Nothing is written to `persistKey` either way, so a widget closed while maximized reopens at its last dragged size. Dragging a `--resize-handle` cancels the maximized state (the next double-press maximizes again instead of restoring). Double-pressing the chevron/✕/extra buttons only does what those buttons do. NOTE there is no `dblclick` event here — the drag cancels `pointerdown`, so Chromium drops mousedown/click/dblclick and the component times the presses itself (400ms, 6px) (src: src/app-modal/FloatingWidgetComp.tsx:38-46,388-441 + `toggleMaximizedWidgetRect` in src/app-modal/floatingWidgetHelpers.ts)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |

| PM-140 | **A slide show over the Webs background list** (src: src/background/BackgroundWebComp.tsx · src/background/backgroundWebCompHelpers.ts `genBackgroundWebDisplayedSrcList` · src/background/backgroundAutoPlayHelpers.ts) | put a web page up from the **[en:tran:Webs]** tab, start the show, let one interval pass; try it with a folder holding saved **URL** items as well as `.html` files; clear the background | the strip appears over the grid once a web page is on a screen and NOT before — no empty row, no rule across the top; the show steps to the next tile AS THE GRID DRAWS IT, files then URLs inside each colour group, and a saved URL is stepped exactly like a file; the badge follows the page that is actually up; clearing the background ends the show on its next tick, the same guard that ends an Images or Videos show. `Wait Until The Video Ends` is not offered here — these are pages, not clips |
| PM-141 | **[en:tran:Effects]** — the dressing fold under _Properties_, on EVERY foreground component (src: src/presenter-foreground/ForegroundDecorationSettingComp.tsx · src/presenter-foreground/foregroundDecorationHelpers.ts) | open any foreground panel → **Properties** → the **Effects** fold; open it, set something, collapse it again | the fold is CLOSED by default and mounts none of its controls while closed; it carries a dot once anything inside it differs from that widget's default, so a look that is set but hidden is still findable. All thirteen values live in ONE setting key per prefix (`<prefix>-setting-show-widget-decoration`) — `appLocalStorage` reads a FILE per key, so a key per property would be thirteen more reads per widget |
| PM-142 | **Effects — [en:tran:Round] / [en:tran:Border] / [en:tran:Shadow] / [en:tran:Padding]**, the four every widget gets (src: src/presenter-foreground/propertiesSettingHelpers.tsx `getWidgetRoundExtraStyle` · foregroundDecorationHelpers.ts `genForegroundDecorationStyle`) | on a text widget AND on a media widget: set a border style + width + colour, a shadow preset, a padding; present it and read the real `screen.html` target | the frame, the fall of shadow and the room round the content all reach the screen, and `box-sizing: border-box` keeps a `Width (%)` honest once padding or a border is on. **Round is the border radius** and it leads the fold — it used to sit among Width/Scale/Opacity and was not applied AT ALL to a widget without geometry, so a marquee had a border it could not round. Defaults: padding `0.25em` on a widget with words and `0` on a media one (no font size, so `em` is meaningless); radius `5px` with geometry and **0 in BOTH halves** without — a pixel size of 0 means "use the percentage", so zeroing only the pixels gives a marquee the 50% default, i.e. a 25% radius it never had |
| PM-143 | **Effects — how the WORDS are set** (`isCommonStyle` widgets only; src: src/presenter-foreground/foregroundDecorationHelpers.ts) | on Messages / a marquee / countdown / clock / quick text: Text Align, Line Height, Letter Spacing, a Text Shadow preset (None/Soft/Glow/**Outline**) and Text Style (italic / underline / UPPERCASE); then open the SAME fold on Video or Image Show | every row reaches the screen, and the text rows are ABSENT on a media widget — a clip has no words to set, and `text-align` on a picture widget is noise in its inline style. Padding, line height and letter spacing are in `em` so a box keeps its shape when **[en:tran:Font Size]** changes; the text shadow is in `em` too, because a 2px outline vanishes under 200px type and swallows a Khmer glyph at 30px. Stacked messages count the padding and the frame, not only the lines, or two notices land on top of each other |
| PM-144 | Background tab **folder sessions** (`MediaSessionsComp` rail) | on **Images**, then **Videos**, **Webs** and **Audios**: read the strip above the list; 🖱️ **＋**; 🖱️ **Select Default "images"** → **Ok**; 🖱️ **Default**; 🖱️R a chip → **Rename Session** / **Remove Session** | each of the four tabs carries `Default` plus a **＋**, and the chips are the SAME control the foreground Image / Video / Web Show widgets carry. A new session starts with NO folder and still shows the strip (it is above the file list, not inside its body — an empty session must be switchable out of). Its folder is written to `<dirSourceSettingName>-<sessionId>` and **Default's own `<dirSourceSettingName>` is left untouched** — that is the whole point, since Path Settings names that one. View mode (PM-114), sort/filter and the slide show follow the session too. Removing forgets ONLY that session's keys and stops its show; the files are never touched. Audios has no slide show, so its rail is the chips alone (src: src/media-sessions/MediaSessionsComp.tsx · src/background/backgroundSessionHelpers.tsx) |
| PM-145 | The background media **rail is ONE short row** (`background-media-bar`) | with a background of that kind on a screen, compare the session chips and the slide-show pill on **Videos**; measure both; check the foreground **Image Show** rail too | the session group and the slide-show pill sit SIDE BY SIDE on one strip, not stacked, and both stand 20px (chips 18px inside a 1px group border) — they must share a baseline. Two stacked strips cost a whole row of thumbnails in a panel that is routinely dragged to 200px. The foreground widgets’ rail is the same height (`.fg-props-toggle` 20px), so **[en:tran:Properties]**, the chips and the show line up there as well (src: src/background/BackgroundMediaComp.tsx · src/background/BackgroundAutoPlayComp.scss · src/media-sessions/mediaSessions.scss · src/presenter-foreground/foregroundProperties.scss) |
| PM-146 | **Sessions on EVERY foreground component** (`MediaSessionsComp` rail via `useForegroundSessions`) | open **[en:tran:Messages]**, **[en:tran:Marquee Top]**, **[en:tran:Marquee Bottom]**, **[en:tran:Quick Text]**, **[en:tran:Countdown]**, **[en:tran:Stopwatch]** and **[en:tran:Time]** in turn: read the strip above **[en:tran:Properties]**; 🖱️ **＋**; type/set something; 🖱️ **Default**; 🖱️ the new chip again | each of the seven carries `Default` plus a **＋**, the SAME control the media widgets and the Background tabs carry. A new session opens on that widget's own defaults — empty Messages, an unticked Rotate, the sample marquee text — and switching back restores the other session's words, numbers AND _Properties_ untouched: every field reads its setting ONCE on mount, so the body is keyed by the session or the previous one's text is written to the new one's keys. **Default's suffix is the empty string**, so it writes the very keys the widget always has (`foreground-message-setting`, `foreground-date-setting`, `marquee-top`…) and nothing an existing install set up moves. **And a session's Properties act on ITS OWN overlay**: with one session's item live, change another session's size, opacity or colour and read the screen's saved style back — it must be untouched, while a change on the owning session must reach it. The refresh used to walk every overlay of that kind, so Session 2's slider re-dressed what Default had on the wall (`toSessionShowingList`) (src: src/presenter-foreground/foregroundSessionHelpers.tsx · src/media-sessions/MediaSessionsComp.tsx) |
| PM-147 | **What a foreground session has ON A SCREEN** (`checkIsSessionData`, `toMessageSessionId`) | on **[en:tran:Messages]**: show an editor from Default, switch to a second session, show one of its editors, read both chips and the Hide row; take each down. Then on **[en:tran:Marquee Bottom]**: show from the second session, switch to Default and show from there | a chip carries the on-screen dot only while THAT session has something up — the one sign of something live belonging to a session nobody is looking at. Messages and Time hold a LIST, so both sessions' items stay up together and each gets its own **[en:tran:Hide Messages]** button naming its text; showing from one session must never drop another's (the panel rewrites the whole list, so anything that is not this session's editors is kept). The single-slot widgets — countdown, stopwatch, quick text, the two marquees — hold ONE entry, so showing from another session REPLACES it and the dot moves; an entry with no session on it (a dropped run-sheet row, the assistant) reads as **Default's**. Removing a session takes what it put up off the screens FIRST — nothing may be left on a projector with no button to hide it |

| RD-09 | `BibleFindPreviewerComp` — results list and chunk footer                   | ⌨️✎ `shepherd` over the KJV; observe `BibleFindRenderPerPageComp`; 🖱️ an unloaded number in the footer, then a loaded one                                      | each hit is a ROW (`app-find-item`, hairline-separated, no per-verse card), its reference a muted marker rather than a bordered pill — the whole row is clickable, so the pill advertised an affordance that was never its own. The matched text carries `app-found-match`: `--app-accent` on its halo with an accent underline, its OWN class since it used to share `app-found-highlight` with that reference and the chunk marker. Each loaded chunk opens with `Results <from>–<to>` (`toFindChunkRange`, counted from ONE — the data's `fromLineNumber` is zero-based for chunk 1 and would print `Results 0–19` under a footer calling it `1`). The footer leads with `N verses found` (`toFoundVerseCount` off `maxLineNumber`) and draws a WINDOW of numbers, never all of them (`toFindPageWindow`): 1556 chunks for a common word used to be 1556 buttons in a 10,260px-tall grid to fill a 100px strip; it is now ~12 until a gap is opened. A loaded chunk is accent-filled and clicking SCROLLS to it; any other is a ghost outline and clicking FETCHES it — the only state this strip has ever carried, where Bootstrap's `.active` said "you are here". The `…` is a BUTTON, not a label: it names the chunks it is holding (`Show pages 4–139`) and opens them, because a number nobody can reach is worse than a number nobody wants to see. An opened gap draws whole up to `FIND_PAGE_EXPAND_LIMIT` (200); past that it opens as evenly spaced steps whose own gaps open the same way, so any chunk of a 1556-chunk find is two clicks off and the strip never grows back into the thousand-button grid. Opened gaps drop when the find changes (the footer is keyed on it), and survive loading a chunk. Sub-controls RD-41..RD-48 (src: src/bible-find/BibleFindRenderDataComp.tsx) |
